page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, it provides dedicated CPU allocation. The processor features 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 260 MB L3 cache. It lacks local storage and bundled GPUs, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place this instance in the average tier for most compute tasks. It achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1672.09 and a multi-core score of 7217.53. In Geekbench testing, it records a single-core score of 1877.0 and a multi-core score of 7215.0, with notable performance in software compilation at 8701.0 and ray tracing at 9855.0. Memory performance shows a read-only small block bandwidth of 568.81 GB/sec, though the PassMark memory score is categorized as weak at 1718.22.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance highly suitable for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. It performs well in static web serving, reaching a throughput of 11.89 GB/sec, and handles Redis SET operations at 8.82 million operations per second. However, memory-intensive tasks or large-scale LLM inference are limited, as shown by a weak text generation speed of 7.92 tokens/sec on a 7B model. This server is best suited for software compilation, web serving, and moderate computational tasks.

Built on the x86_64 architecture with an Intel processor, it features 4 physical cores, 2 threads per core, and a 260 MB L3 cache. The instance does not include local storage or a GPU. Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7215.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 7217.53.
